A short guide to travel paperwork for customers
What you should know comes first
Travel paperwork for companion animals

At Aurelia Skyways, the Companion Animal Travel Desk keeps the paperwork side of travel clear and steady. This guide covers the records most travelers need before departure, so you can arrive prepared and avoid last-minute delays. Safety takes priority over speed in every journey, and the right documents help us care for each animal with confidence.

Please keep your booking record, vaccination papers, and any health certificate that applies to your route in one place. If your animal travels in the cabin or in the hold, the paperwork should still match the reservation details exactly. Small differences in a name, breed description, or contact note can slow review, so check everything before you set out.

Some journeys call for extra approval from a vet, an import office, or another authority. If you are traveling with Mateo Morgan, Theo Torres, or Fluffy, the same record checks still apply, and a clear folder makes the handoff easier. You do not need to separate your items by category unless a local rule asks for that, but it helps to keep originals and copies together.

At the desk, staff may ask for proof that your pet is fit to travel and that all required vaccinations are current. <<FACT F019>> Bring any note that explains medication, feeding needs, or handling concerns, since these details help us support the animal during the trip. If you have questions about a form, ask before the day of travel so the records can be reviewed with care.

For routes that involve inspection or transfer, additional papers may be requested at check-in or at arrival. <<FACT F028>> Keep your contact information easy to read, and make sure the person meeting the animal at the destination has what they need.

If your papers are incomplete, the journey may be delayed while the missing items are confirmed. The Companion Animal Travel Desk can help you prepare the right records and point you to the next step.
